title: Complete Tomato Processing Plant Solutions
overviewDescription: Industrial tomato processing is not forgiving. You either capture the colour, viscosity, and microbial stability at the right moment or you lose them permanently. A tomato line that runs at 20 tons per hour cannot afford inconsistent enzyme inactivation, pressure drops across the evaporator, or contamination in the sterile filler. Every stage is interdependent.
overviewsubDescription: At SEPPA, we approach every tomato processing plant the way we engineer dairy lines where hygiene protocol, thermal precision, and product consistency are non negotiable manufacturing requirements. With over 7,000 installations worldwide and 50 years of complete line experience, we build integrated systems that run from fresh tomato reception to aseptic pouch or bottle filling without breaking the chain of control.

What SEPPA delivers is not a collection of standalone machines. It is a complete, engineered tomato line feasibility study, process layout, fabrication, installation, and commissioning built to the same sanitary standard you would expect from a top tier dairy processing plant.
featuresTitle: Key Equipment in a Tomato Processing Plant
featuresSubtitle: The performance of any tomato line depends entirely on the precision of its thermal and mechanical units. The equipment SEPPA fabricates in 304 and 316L stainless steel mirrors the sanitary standards found in dairy processing plants where surface finish, weld quality, and dead-leg elimination are mandatory, not optional.

features.title: Hot/Cold Break Units
features.description: The break point determines your product. SEPPA's tubular and plate heat exchangers deliver rapid, consistent enzyme inactivation whether you are running a cold break tomato line at 68–70°C or a hot break system at 88–95°C. Temperature uniformity across the product cross-section is held within +1°C, the same precision standard applied in milk pasteurization systems.

features.title: Multi Effect Vacuum Evaporators
features.description: Concentration without degradation. SEPPA's falling film evaporators operate at 45–55°C under vacuum, protecting colour, flavour, and lycopene stability during Brix concentration. Triple effect configurations reduce steam consumption by up to 60% compared to single-effect systems economics that a traditional dairy production line engineer will recognize immediately.

features.title: Aseptic Filling and Packaging Lines
features.description: For the tomato ketchup production line and tomato sauce production line, SEPPA integrates aseptic fillers bags in box, pouches, and PET bottles fabricated to the same sterility standards that govern a dairy production line for UHT milk. Our PET bottle engineering reduces bottle weight by 25% while increasing top load strength by more than 30%, combining structural integrity with material savings.

features.title: CIP Systems and Hygienic Transfer Pumps
features.description: No facility runs clean without a well engineered CIP circuit. SEPPA installs centralized or satellite CIP systems with conductivity verification and time temperature logging, consistent with the dairy processing equipment standards applied across our global installations.

contentBlocks.title: Applications of Tomato Processing Lines
paragraphs: The versatility of the tomato processing line is what makes it commercially valuable and technically demanding. Tomato paste at 28–30° Brix is a completely different product from a tomato ketchup production line running at 1.5% salt, 25% sugar, and 0.5% acetic acid. A tomato sauce production line targeting 8–12° Brix for ambient retail shelf requires different thermal holding times, different viscosity management, and a different packaging format compared to a bulk aseptic drum filling operation.

SEPPA's complete tomato line handles all of these: Cold break paste (68–75°C) for higher lycopene retention and brighter colour, Hot break paste (85–95°C) for higher viscosity and pectin activation, Diced and whole peeled tomato lines with blanching and brine injection, Tomato sauce production line for retail glass or PET bottling, Tomato ketchup production line with inline Brix, pH, and viscosity control, Bulk aseptic filling for food industry intermediate supply.
Matching this range to a single integrated facility with shared CIP systems, shared utilities, and a common SCADA layer is exactly what SEPPA's engineering team designs and delivers.

contentBlocks.title: Tomato Processing Workflow: From Fresh Tomatoes to Finished Products
paragraphs: Step 1: Fruit Reception and Sorting - Tomatoes arrive by truck and enter the tomato line through hydraulic flume conveying. Optical sorters and roller graders eliminate diseased, green, or bruised fruit before the first thermal stage. Yield at reception directly affects Brix input to the evaporator.

Step 2: Washing and Scalding - A three-stage rotary drum washer removes field soil, pesticide residue, and surface microbes. Immediately after washing, tomatoes enter the break unit. The break temperature hot or cold defines the enzyme profile of everything downstream in the process.

Step 3: Break and Pulping - SEPPA's break and finisher system uses a cascade of screens (0.8mm, 0.5mm, 0.4mm) to separate juice and pulp from seeds and skin. The finisher yield directly impacts your output solids. SEPPA's screen geometry consistently outperforms industry averages for pulp extraction efficiency.

Step 4: Evaporation and Concentration - The clarified juice enters the vacuum evaporator. For a facility producing 28–30° Brix paste, a multi effect evaporator at correct vacuum levels handles 8–10 kg of evaporation per kg of steam consumed. SEPPA's falling film design protects the colour sensitive compounds that turn paste brown when overheated.

Step 5: Formulation (for Ketchup and Sauce Lines) - In the process of making tomato ketchup, the concentrate paste is mixed with sugar, vinegar, salt, starch, and spice oleoresins in stainless steel blending tanks with high shear mixers. The Brix meter, pH meter, and viscosity meter work inline and send readings to the SCADA, which makes automatic corrections in real time.

Step 6: Pasteurization and Sterile Filling - The finished product passes through a tubular or scraped surface heat exchanger for final pasteurization, then enters the sterile zone. SEPPA integrates aseptic fillers for bag in box (up to 1,000L aseptic drums), pouches, and PET bottles. Every seal, every gasket, and every valve is specified to 3-A sanitary standards.

whyChoose.title: Why Choose SEPPA for Tomato Processing Lines?
paragraphs: Companies that have previously operated dairy production lines find SEPPA's tomato line systems immediately familiar in terms of sanitary discipline and noticeably more automated in terms of process control.

SEPPA has been designing and manufacturing complete lines for over 50 years. More than 7,000 installations globally. The systems we build today incorporate SCADA based automation, servo controlled filling, and integrated vision inspection that most conventional tomato operations have not yet adopted.

For the tomato sauce production line, that means continuous pasteurizer temperature logging with automatic diversion on deviation. For bulk paste operations, it means aseptic drum filling with a validated sterility assurance level.

Companies transitioning from dairy plant environments appreciate that the engineering logic is the same: control the thermal profile, eliminate contamination risk, and measure everything continuously. Whether the output is a tomato sauce production line for retail jars or bulk aseptic paste, SEPPA applies that same discipline at scale.

methodology.title: How SEPPA Designs and Builds Your Tomato Processing Plant

steps.title: Phase 1: Feasibility and Process Design
steps.description: Every project engagement begins with a process feasibility study: raw material Brix input, targeted output specification, daily tonnage, available utilities, and packaging format. SEPPA engineers use this data to define the mass and energy balance before a single piece of equipment is specified.

steps.title: Phase 2: CAD Layout and Engineering
steps.description: Full 3D CAD modeling of the facility layout. Pipe routing, vessel placement, CIP circuit design, and electrical panel positioning are all finalized before fabrication begins.

steps.title: Phase 3: Fabrication
steps.description: All vessels, evaporator bodies, and piping are fabricated in house in 304/316L stainless steel. Internal surface finish Ra ≤ 0.8 µm. Full passivation and pressure testing on every unit before it leaves the factory.

steps.title: Phase 4: Installation and Commissioning
steps.description: SEPPA's field engineers handle mechanical installation, process piping, and electrical integration. Commissioning runs a full qualification protocol IQ, OQ, PQ before handing over the tomato line to the client's production team.

steps.title: Phase 5: After Sales Service and Spare Support
steps.description: Stocking of spare parts, diagnostic systems from a distance by SCADA, and local servicing personnel are available worldwide. The post sale service provision system of SEPPA is designed to satisfy the same uptime requirements.

faqs.question: Can the tomato processing plant scale from 5 to 50 tons per hour?
faqs.answer: Yes. SEPPA designs these systems as modular capacity blocks. A 5 TPH starter tomato line can be expanded by adding evaporator effects, increasing finisher screen count, and upgrading the aseptic filler speed without replacing the base architecture. This is the same scalability approach applied to dairy production line expansions.

faqs.question: Does the tomato processing line meet the same sanitary standards as dairy processing equipment?
faqs.answer: The SEPPA tomato processing line is built according to the 3-A and EHEDG standards that are required for dairy production systems. Surface finish, dead leg removal, and CIP validation are deliverables, and not options.

faqs.question: How does automation on the tomato ketchup production line compare to a dairy production line?
faqs.answer: A modern SEPPA tomato ketchup production line uses inline Brix, pH, viscosity, and colour sensors feeding a closed loop SCADA system comparable in automation density to a high end dairy production line. Manual intervention is reduced to raw material input and packaging changeovers.

faqs.question: What is the ROI timeline for a dedicated tomato processing plant versus a multi product facility?
faqs.answer: A dedicated facility typically delivers faster ROI than a multi product setup because it optimizes CIP frequency, reduces changeover losses, and allows continuous season processing. For a 20 TPH hot break tomato line, payback periods of 3–5 years are common in markets with a reliable raw material supply.

faqs.question: How does SEPPA handle spare parts and service outside India?
faqs.answer: SEPPA maintains regional service hubs and pre stocked spare part inventories for all major tomato line components pumps, screens, seals, sensors, and filling valves. Remote SCADA access allows our engineers to diagnose faults and push parameter corrections without a site visit in most cases.
